findings.claim: Nothing in the suite pins the two attribute guards as independent: all five tests move `username` and `locale` together, so the case the ticket's second half is about (locale changes while the username does not) is unasserted, and a plausible later refactor to a single combined guard passes the whole class.
findings.evidence: Mutation experiment at d381957e84386f5902bec7886b8f2ba391dc5101: replaced the two setSessionAttributeIfChanged calls in OpenmrsFilter.java:93-94 with one combined guard keyed only on the username (`if (!Objects.equals(httpSession.getAttribute("username"), username)) { setAttribute("username",...); setAttribute("locale",...); }`) and ran `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` -> `Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` (log: scratchpad/ab-6555/mutant-run.log). The mutant survives, so the suite does not cover a locale-only change. That the scenario is real is stated in-tree: UserContext.getLocale() (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/UserContext.java:350-356) deliberately returns LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale() uncached with the comment "don't cache default locale - allows recognition of changed default at login page", i.e. an anonymous session's locale can change between requests while its username stays "-anonymous user-"; for an authenticated session Context.setLocale(Locale) (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/Context.java:880) delegates to UserContext.setLocale and is the mid-session language switch. Suggested test: a second request on the same session after the locale changed, asserting countWrites(USERNAME)==0, countWrites(LOCALE)==1 and the new Locale value. Production file restored with `git checkout --`; worktree verified clean.

findings.claim: The `@AfterEach logout()` never logs anything out - every test in the class runs doFilterInternal, whose `finally { Context.clearUserContext(); }` removes the thread-local, so Context.logout() returns at its `if (!isSessionOpen()) return;` guard; the teardown implies an isolation step that does not happen.
findings.evidence: Probe run at head: temporarily printed Context.isSessionOpen() from the @AfterEach and ran `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest='OpenmrsFilterTest#doFilterInternal_shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale'` -> `PROBE_A isSessionOpen_at_AfterEach=false` (log: scratchpad/ab-6555/probe-run.log). Mechanism: Context.userContextHolder is a plain ThreadLocal with no initialValue (api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/context/Context.java:145), clearUserContext() calls remove() (Context.java:245), isSessionOpen() is `userContextHolder.get() != null` (Context.java:971), and Context.logout() early-returns on !isSessionOpen(). The same guard also skips the base class's own cleanup at api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/test/jupiter/BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:992-1001 (`if (Context.isSessionOpen()) Context.logout();`). No live harm found: ran the class ahead of two sibling context-sensitive web tests in one JVM (`mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest='OpenmrsFilterTest,FilterUtilTest,AltAuthSchemeContextTest' -Dsurefire.runOrder=reversealphabetical`) - all 11 tests green, so nothing leaks today. Either drop the dead @AfterEach or move the Context.logout() where it can still run. Test file restored with `git checkout --`.

findings.claim: The new 17-line dataset, getTestUserCredentials(), and the two executeDataSet/Context.authenticate pairs are not needed - BaseContextSensitiveTest already authenticates every test as `admin`, so the authenticated tests work unchanged against the existing fixtures.
findings.evidence: Probe run at head: deleted `executeDataSet(FILTER_INITIAL_DATA_XML)` and `Context.authenticate(getTestUserCredentials())` from doFilterInternal_shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale and changed the expectation to "admin"; `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest='OpenmrsFilterTest#doFilterInternal_shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale'` -> `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0`, with `PROBE_B isAuthenticated_at_test_start=true user=admin` (log: scratchpad/ab-6555/probe-run.log). Base class: getCredentials() returns admin/test (api/src/test/java/org/openmrs/test/jupiter/BaseContextSensitiveNonTransactionalTest.java:386-388) and baseSetupWithStandardDataAndAuthentication() calls authenticate() before every test (same file, ~line 963-998). The added users row is a byte-for-byte copy of api/src/test/resources/org/openmrs/api/include/AdministrationServiceTest-globalproperties.xml:27, and it now lives on master plus the 2.9.x/2.8.x/2.7.x backports. what_i_swept: Enumerated the behavior changes in web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java by diffing the full base and head files (not just hunks): (1) a repeat request with unchanged values now performs zero setAttribute calls; (2) an authenticated request writes `username` once instead of writing the anonymous placeholder then overwriting it; (3) a repeat authenticated request performs zero writes. Verified each against the base EMPIRICALLY rather than by reading: overwrote OpenmrsFilter.java with the merge-base version (eda229b12a28a41ba35ecd75b910803da93631a8) while keeping the PR's tests, then `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` -> `Tests run: 5, Failures: 3`, failing exactly doFilterInternal_shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAnonymousSessionAttributes (expected 0, got 1), doFilterInternal_shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes (expected 0, got 2) and doFilterInternal_shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale (expected 1, got 2). So all three behavior changes have a differentiating test that asserts the runtime effect (real setAttribute calls counted through a MockHttpSession subclass), not a proxy. The other two tests pass on base and are legitimate characterization coverage for the ticket's first acceptance criterion ("attributes end up with the same values as today"). Head is green: `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest` -> 5/5. Then probed for gaps the green suite hides, with a mutation experiment (combined guard keyed on username only) that the suite fails to kill -> finding 1. Checked branch/line coverage of the new code from the head run's jacoco.xml: setSessionAttributeIfChanged 3/3 lines, 2/2 branches; doFilterInternal 24/27 lines, 5/6 branches (the missed branch is the pre-existing csrfguard URI check). Outward trace, four directions. (a) Consumers of the two session attributes: `git grep 'getAttribute("username")'` returns nothing anywhere in the repo and `getAttribute("locale")` returns exactly one hit, web/src/test/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/initialization/InitializationFilterE2ETest.java:109 (a different filter, unaffected) - the single hit is the positive control that the zero-hit username search is real. So no existing test asserted the old per-request-write behavior and none needed updating. (b) Session listeners: only web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java, which is a ServletContextListener, not an attribute listener, so no notification contract depends on the dropped writes. (c) Test-suite neighbours: ran the new class ahead of two sibling BaseWebContextSensitiveTest subclasses in one surefire JVM with -Dsurefire.runOrder=reversealphabetical - all green, no cross-class Context pollution, which downgraded finding 2 from a possible correctness problem to test hygiene. (d) The shipped branches: all four commits named in the JIRA (master merge 645814dc, 2.9.x f0dc84a9, 2.8.x 7d3d2c78, 2.7.x b25424255) carry OpenmrsFilterTest.java +244 and the fixture +17, and the 2.8.x/2.7.x copies are correctly adapted to javax.servlet - no branch received the behavior change without its tests. Every file I mutated for evidence was restored with `git checkout --` and `git status --porcelain` is empty; no probe classes were created.

Whether a downstream consumer (legacy UI, a distributed session manager) depends on the per-request write itself rather than on the attribute value - the repo contains no reader of either attribute, but modules outside openmrs-core were not searched.
